chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
There is no harm in performing wudu from (water) from which an animal whose flesh is permissible to eat has drunk.

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no harm/objection — a standard jurisprudential formula indicating permissibility
key_terms.مَا يُؤْكَلُ لَحْمُهُ: That whose flesh is lawfully eaten — i.e., halal animals
key_terms.يُتَوَضَّأَ: Performing wudu (ritual ablution) — the minor purification required before salat

ai.seo_question: Can you perform wudu with water that a permissible animal has drunk from?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) rules that water from which a halal animal (such as cattle, sheep, or poultry) has drunk remains ritually pure and valid for wudu. This is a foundational ruling in Shia fiqh on tahara (ritual purity). The chapter addresses whether the saliva or mouth contact of various creatures renders water impure — here the Imam affirms that permissible animals (those whose flesh is lawful to eat) do not contaminate such water.
